correctness.rationale: The two distances are (sqrt(3)/2)|t| and (sqrt(3)/2)|1-t|. Taking the farther line and projecting gives the stated two affine branches; both chart descriptions of a vertex give the same opposite midpoint. On t>1 two steps give t/4, and on t<0 they give 1+(t-1)/4. Iterating to [0,1] exhausts all exterior states; the two open half-sides remain invariant and contract by -1/2 per step toward the two three-cycles. The endpoints and midpoint are precisely the exceptions in [0,1]; pulling these back by the two-step maps gives the stated four progressions and the midpoint. Across each such point, nearby iterates on opposite sides land in different invariant half-sides. The progressions give 4 log_4 R+O(1) per chart, and shared vertices affect the distinct count by O(1). The positive-ray minus basin occupies (0,1/2) and (4^k,2·4^k); adding their clipped lengths gives the boxed formula, with a continuous phase rising to 2/3 and falling to 1/3 on [1,4]. This is for complete lines and directed cutoffs, not all cutoff conventions. The frozen verifier reports finite checks, not an independent audit. A separate bounded check (python /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 4) agreed for 1,887 exact rational geometric orbits; it is not a proof for all real states.
